newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Old fear hits Euro shares in new year.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Old fear hits Euro shares in new year.

text.p: The fear of rising interest rates resurfaced on Thursday to chop more than one percent off Europe's key bourses in the first minutes of new year trading after Wall Street ended the old year by losing 101 points.
German shares were down 1.8 percent, French shares by 1.7 percent and London, Europe's busiest market, by around one percent at 1000 gmt, though levels then rallied a touch.

"It's the same old story -- the fear of rising interest rates," said one London share dealer. "Given that we finished the year in a fairly strong fashion, I think we could see a rather substantial markdown and perhaps finish the day one to two percent lower."

Wall Street shares fell 101.10 points, or 1.5 percent, to 6,448.27 on Tuesday -- the biggest one-day drop since mid-July -- as bond yields rose to 6.64 percent from 6.54 percent on Monday on a brace of stronger-than-expected U.S. economic indicators.

The U.S. government said sales of new homes jumped a stronger-than-expected 14.2 percent in November, the steepest rise in more than 3-1/2 years. In addition, consumer confidence soared in December, jumping to a reading of 113.8 from 109.5 in November, the Conference Board said.

Traders fear that the strength of U.S. economic growth could signal a rise in inflation and lead to higher interest rates, which spell bad news for highly valued share markets as returns on other investments and holding cash on deposit rise.

Tuesday's drop put a small dent in Wall Street's rise for 1996 but coupled with its 1995 performance, the Dow has climbed around 60 percent over the last two years, a run the likes of which has been seen only twice before, in 1927-28 and 1954-55.
The market's gains in 1996 came despite widespread predictions that inflation or weak corporate earnings would rain on Wall Street's parade.
European shares chased U.S. shares higher in 1996 when British stocks chalked up a gain of 11.6 percent, Frankfurt 28 percent and French shares almost 24 percent.
While the mood was more cautious on Thursday, many traders were still on holiday and business was relatively thin.

Technical analysts in London viewed the fall as simply a correction in a bull market and pegged near-term chart support for the FTSE at 4,065, with further support at 4,050 and major psychological support at 4,000.
Frence's CAC-40 index of leading shares opened down 0.43 percent and then fell further with the losses exaggerated in thin post-holiday trade.

German shares fell the most but dealers said they did not expect any further strong declines amid particularly weak trading volumes. They also said the slight recovery of the dollar was supportive for German shares.
Currency dealers said the dollar's momentum was to the upside though business was thin.
"It is quite well bid. But there is no corporate interest around," said a trader at a British bank.
The dollar has recovered steam in Europe after the fall in U.S. stocks and bonds pushed it to lows of 115.55 yen and 1.5358 marks in late dealings on January 31.
Dollar-yen was trading at 115.99 against 115.85 in late Europe on Tuesday. The yen has is under pressure against the dollar on concerns over the strength of Japan economy.

World oil prices began 1997 with a rally as freezing weather continued to grip much of Europe, stoking demand for winter heating oil and memories of a similar cold snap in the United States a year ago.
The February Brent crude oil futures contract on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) was up 56 cents a barrel at $24.37 by 1030 GMT from the closing price of 1996.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.5477 marks and 115.99 yen compared with 1.5385 marks and 115.85 yen late on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British fell 40.5 points to 4,078.0.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index fell 40.06 points to 2,275.67.
In Frankfurt, the 30-share DAX index fell 54.47 points to 2834.22 points. PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $367.80 compared with its late level of $369.05 in London on Tuesday.
